item.title: 'Shopping for free': Students loot LPU campus mall; torch computer science block
item.description: Several videos from Lovely Professional University show students reportedly taking items from shops during protests. The protests were sparked by allegations surrounding the rape of a female student and a student's suicide. Police reported clashes, stone-pelting, and damage to property during the unrest, escalated by social media rumors. An investigation has been initiated, while the university has denied the rape allegations as false.
item.dc:creator: SHREEDHAR RATHI

item.title: Bloodbath at D-Street: Why is stock market down today? Top reasons explained
item.description: Stock market crash today: While Sensex crashed over 1,000 points, Nifty50 went below 22,850. At 10:40 AM, Nifty50 was trading at 22,835.15, down 305 points or 1.32%. BSE Sensex was at 72,909.34, down 986 points or 1.33%.
item.dc:creator: SMRITI JAIN

item.title: Bill Gates Foundation to shut down in 2045: Why some Americans reject its $400m ‘gift’
item.description: The Bill Gates Foundation is making a bold move by committing $1 billion to ensure equitable AI development for education and healthcare. Of this, $400 million is dedicated to creating AI-driven tutoring systems that tailor learning experiences. This investment arrives amidst rising discussions about digital tools' effectiveness and privacy issues, with New York City already enacting a one-year pause on generative AI in schools.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Anushka lets daughter binge at ice-cream museum, shares parenting lesson
item.description: During a recent visit to a museum, Anushka Sharma let her daughter Vamika enjoy some ice cream. Interestingly, Vamika showed restraint and didn’t overindulge, despite the absence of strict food rules. Anushka highlighted that discussing food choices effectively fosters understanding and promotes healthier eating habits, illustrating that teaching kids about nutrition can be a enjoyable journey.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.dc:creator: PRIYANKA JAISWAL

item.title: The 1066 real estate revolution: How one man reshaped land ownership in England
item.description: William, Duke of Normandy, invaded England in 1066, leading to significant changes in land ownership. Following his victory over King Harold II, William redistributed land among his supporters. The creation of the Domesday Book in 1086 recorded land ownership and resources in the realm. By the end of William's reign, Norman nobles held the majority of England's wealth and land. This transformed the English feudal structure and increased taxation efficiency.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: 'We have a serious problem': CJP's Abhijeet Dipke reacts to LPU unrest
item.description: Protests erupted at Lovely Professional University in Punjab following allegations of a rape committed on campus. Students vandalized property and clashed with police, resulting in several injuries and damaged vehicles. In response to the unrest, the university suspended classes for ten days and advised students to stay indoors. A police investigation into the alleged rape is underway, while the university denied the claims as rumors.
item.dc:creator: HADI KHAN

item.title: Cleaners react with ozone, filling homes with lung-deep nanoparticles
item.description: A study conducted at Purdue University reveals that scented cleaning products release compounds that react with indoor ozone, leading to the quick formation of ultrafine particles that may diminish air quality. During cleaning in confined areas, these particles can accumulate significantly. While maintaining cleanliness is essential, it is wise to minimize exposure to chemical byproducts through methods like opting for fragrance-free alternatives and ensuring adequate ventilation.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Girl started lemonade stand with $10 goal; 7 summers later, sisters raised $55,000
item.description: Grace Hendrian and her sister June initiated their Lemon-Aid Stand for Good in 2019 to support charity. They aimed to raise $10 but ultimately collected $55,000 for The Salvation Army. Their project encouraged community participation, leading to 14 stands operating by 2026. The sisters received recognition for their volunteer efforts as they also contributed to local families in need. Their fundraising initiative concluded in 2026, marking its final season.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Scientists dumped 1,500 Christmas trees in a lake to transform its ecosystem
item.description: In an innovative study in southeastern Finland, researchers submerged 1,500 spruce trees in Lake Saimaa to analyze their influence on aquatic biodiversity. After a three-year period, the findings revealed a marked increase in benthic organisms. This experiment showcases how discarded Christmas trees could be creatively repurposed to foster healthier underwater ecosystems, shedding light on sustainable waste management strategies.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: California acquires 640 acres near Pioneertown to save western Joshua trees
item.description: California state officials secured 640 acres of desert land near Pioneertown for western Joshua tree conservation. Researchers identified this land as suitable for the species despite climate change. The California Department of Fish and Wildlife completed the acquisition with funds from the Western Joshua Tree Conservation Fund. Collaboration with Native American tribes is planned for long-term stewardship of the property.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Yellowstone-to-Yukon project builds 204 crossings, saves 24M hectares
item.description: The Yellowstone to Yukon Conservation Initiative is proudly nominated for Prince William's Earthshot Prize in 2026. This groundbreaking effort aims to reinstate a vital 3,400-kilometre wildlife corridor through the majestic Rocky Mountains. Achieving over 200 wildlife crossings and safeguarding around 24 million hectares, Indigenous involvement is key to strengthening conservation practices here. Looking forward, the initiative hopes to secure an extra 20 million hectares by 2030.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Yellowstone rangers pulled 20,100 items from geysers, including 280 hats
item.description: Yellowstone rangers removed more than 20,100 pieces of trash from geothermal areas in 2026, along with over 5,000 rocks and sticks and 280 visitor hats. Staff also collected coins worth more than $18. Among the unusual finds were AirPods, golf tees, an inhaler, Invisalign retainers, fake nails and children’s toys.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: America’s first new nuclear warhead in nearly four decades
item.description: The United States is making strides in its W93 nuclear warhead initiative, in collaboration with the Navy. This modern program seeks to revitalize the submarine-launched ballistic missile capability after over thirty years of stagnation. Designed to increase operational flexibility, the W93/Mk7 warhead will bolster the nation's nuclear deterrent at sea. It has now entered the crucial Engineering and Manufacturing Development stage, signifying a pivotal advancement.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.dc:creator: PRIYANKA JAISWAL

item.title: 'Bhai, meri injury ho gayi hai': How Neeraj's call landed Yashvir an Asiad spot
item.description: After Neeraj Chopra’s injury opened the door to his Asian Games opportunity, the Indian athlete received a call from the star javelin thrower, who encouraged him to make the chance count. From motivating him before the competition to speaking ahead of his final throw, Chopra remained a source of support. Having worked extensively on his technique and fitness, the athlete now heads into the Asian Games dreaming of delivering his best performance.
item.dc:creator: AMIT KUMAR

item.title: Man slapped by Parvesh Verma was out on bail in MCD worker abduction, assault case
item.description: Delhi PWD Minister Parvesh Verma was involved in a confrontation with Sahib Singh over a newly laid road. Sahib Singh was previously released on bail for allegedly assaulting an MCD sanitation worker. During the incident, AAP MLA Jarnail Singh questioned the road's quality and recorded the inspection. After Verma slapped Singh, AAP leaders protested, demanding his arrest and accountability.
item.dc:creator: SHREEDHAR RATHI

item.title: Louisiana neighbors' fight over 70-foot strip ends with $15K, dead cow stunt
item.description: In a prolonged conflict stemming from years of camaraderie, two families in Louisiana found themselves locked in a bitter legal battle regarding their property lines. The Colvins asserted ownership over a disputed 70-foot timberland strip, triggering rising tensions. Ultimately, the court sided with the Joneses, affirming the original boundary marked by an aged fence while ordering the Colvins to halt disruptive actions and compensate for damages.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: $45M SF mansion linked to Ellison sells to investor after year of secrecy
item.description: Private equity mogul Chuck Esserman has made headlines by purchasing a lavish mansion in San Francisco for $45 million, making it the most expensive home sale in the city for 2025. Formerly owned by Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, who bought it for just $3.9 million 37 years ago, the estate boasts stunning renovations and breathtaking views of the Golden Gate Bridge, reflecting its rich legacy.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Ex-elite runner turned nun raises $2.6M in Chicago Marathon for families
item.description: Sister Stephanie Baliga once dreamed of becoming an elite runner before finding her calling as a nun. She has since used the Chicago Marathon to raise more than $2.6 million for Mission of Our Lady of the Angels, helping feed families in need. Now, she continues running and fundraising through Team OLA.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Kids need boundaries over freedom to build self-control: Psychology
item.description: Guiding children towards self-regulation requires parents to create clear and consistent boundaries throughout their growth. This means offering structure while also granting children the freedom to make choices. Studies indicate that the perfect blend of emotional support and steady expectations nurtures vital executive function skills. As children develop, boundaries can evolve, promoting their ability to control behaviors independently.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Owner left punctured BMW, later it caught fire. Court backs his Rs 70 lakh claim
item.description: Maharashtra state consumer commission ruled that United India Insurance must compensate a BMW owner after a claim rejection. The car was destroyed by fire following a late-night tyre puncture, leading to the owner seeking compensation. The commission determined that the owner's actions constituted reasonable precautions under the circumstances. The insurer's refusal was deemed a deficiency in service without sufficient justification.
item.dc:creator: SAURABH THAKUR

item.dc:creator: KANCHAN YADAV

item.title: Israel minister Ben-Gvir threatens to execute jailed Hamas figure
item.description: Itamar Ben-Gvir confronted Hamas operative Hassan Salameh in an Israeli prison, where Salameh is serving time for his involvement in lethal attacks. In a dramatic moment he described as closure, Ben-Gvir expressed his wish for Salameh to face execution. This incident underlines Ben-Gvir’s hardline approach to security regarding Palestinian prisoners, especially following recent legislation pushing for the death penalty for terrorists in military courts.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: Toll soars to 81 as UP is lashed by 775% excess rainfall in 48 hours
item.description: In a mere 48 hours, torrential rainfall hit Uttar Pradesh, causing devastating consequences that claimed 81 lives and injured 62. The districts of Sitapur, Lakhimpur Kheri, and Bahraich faced the brunt of the disasters. Current rescue operations are focused on evaluating the extensive destruction of property and crops, while officials are mobilizing to offer support to those affected.
item.dc:creator: ARVIND CHAUHAN

item.title: At 21°C, Delhi records its lowest minimum temperature in Sept in 18 years
item.description: Delhi experienced its lowest minimum temperature in 18 years, reaching 21 degrees Celsius, which is three notches below normal. The India Meteorological Department reported that heavy rain and storms in surrounding states contributed to the cool weather. Various locations in Delhi also recorded significantly low temperatures, with Ridge at 16.8 degrees Celsius. While the maximum temperature at Safdarjung was recorded at 30.6 degrees Celsius, it remained four notches below normal.
item.dc:creator: KUSHAGRA DIXIT

item.title: Judge orders revival of $7B Solar for All program, says EPA overstepped
item.description: A Rhode Island federal judge has ordered the revival of the $7 billion Solar for All program after the Trump administration’s EPA canceled it in August 2025. Judge Mary S. McElroy ruled the agency overstepped its authority in terminating the Biden-era initiative, which aimed to expand solar access for low-income households nationwide.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: 14-year-old Georgia student scores perfect 1600 on SAT
item.description: At just 14 years old, Ashrit Talluri from Georgia has achieved remarkable success, scoring a flawless 1600 on the SAT exam. Having earned 14½ high school credits in middle school, he is now taking college-level courses as a ninth grader at Innovation Academy. With five months of meticulous preparation behind him, Ashrit dreams of becoming a neurosurgeon, eager to delve into projects that combine cutting-edge technology with healthcare.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Blind at 8, auto driver's son cracks UPSC with AIR 109
item.description: Ajay R Raj faced the heartbreaking challenge of losing most of his sight early in life, compounded by financial struggles within his family. Yet, a library became his refuge, igniting his passion for literature. With relentless dedication, he excelled academically and chased his dream, eventually gaining admission to St. Stephen's College in Delhi. His relentless pursuit through several attempts at the UPSC exam showcased his resilience.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: 'Crushed man's head with stones': How murder accused evaded arrest for 24 years
item.description: A man named Firoj has been arrested after evading capture for 24 years. He was accused of murdering Kalaam Ansari due to a family vendetta. The incident occurred in February 2002 when Ansari's decomposed body was found in a DDA forest. Investigation revealed that Ansari had moved to Delhi for work with Firoj, who later committed the crime. The case highlights the challenges faced in resolving long-standing criminal investigations.
item.dc:creator: G S DHANUSH

item.title: Connor McDavid, Lauren Kyle support kids through cancer care and youth sports
item.description: Connor McDavid continues his support for the Ben Stelter Foundation, helping families affected by childhood cancer. In January 2026, he attended a fundraiser at Allendale School, highlighting community efforts and the foundation's purpose. Meanwhile, Lauren Kyle serves on the Edmonton Oilers Community Foundation board, promoting youth sport accessibility through initiatives. Their charitable work addresses different issues, yet both focus on benefiting children and families.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: LeBron James opens up on raising his three children with Savannah James
item.description: LeBron James, the NBA legend, has reflected on being a father to his children and teaching them about life.
